title: Post-seal experimental agreement of the inverse-square exponent
statement: After the Fold structure independently forces and seals positive integer exponent two, the Williams, Faller and Hill Coulomb-law experiment reports q = (2.7 +/- 3.1) x 10^-16 in the tested form 1/r^(2+q).  Converting only the reported finite interval to exact positive rational exponent bounds and enumerating every positive integer inside them leaves two as the sole compatible exponent.
generation_rule: Generate the complete product of physical carrier, inverse-square relation, provenance, capability-closed prediction, separate measurement record, complete rows, positive-successor closure and no-extra-rule forms.
grammar_boundary: All exact post-seal comparisons between the forced positive integer exponent and the complete finite positive exponent interval reported by the registered primary experiment.

choices.name: answer-only-scalar
choices.reason: An answer-only scalar erases the generated physical carrier.

choices.name: complete-fold-carrier
choices.reason: The complete Fold trace retains the observed physical distinction.

choices.name: imported-or-fitted-relation
choices.reason: An imported or fitted relation lets consensus or target data select the law.

choices.name: forced-exponent-two-versus-complete-reported-interval
choices.reason: The structural exponent is sealed first; the complete source-bound interval is then converted to exact positive rational endpoints and exhaustively checked for compatible positive integers.

choices.name: unbound-provenance
choices.reason: Unbound provenance cannot demonstrate which premises produced the result.

choices.name: source-bound-proof-trace
choices.reason: Every generated candidate and decision is bound to its exact source trace.

choices.name: target-readable-prediction
choices.reason: A target-readable predictor can copy or optimize against the measurement.

choices.name: capability-closed-prediction
choices.reason: The registered Fold instruction surface has no target or ambient host capability.

choices.name: proof-measurement-conflation
choices.reason: Treating an external decimal record as a proof scalar violates the measured-value boundary.

choices.name: separate-measurement-record
choices.reason: External values remain source-bound records compared only after sealing.

choices.name: selected-favourable-rows
choices.reason: Selecting favorable rows cannot falsify the relation.

choices.name: complete-registered-rows
choices.reason: Every favorable, unfavorable and tampered registered row is retained.

choices.name: finite-answer-lookup
choices.reason: An answer lookup has no successor certificate.

choices.name: one-successor-closure
choices.reason: The One base and generated successor preserve the relation at every declared finite depth.

choices.name: free-extra-rule
choices.reason: A free constant, scale or exception can select the measured answer.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: No rule beyond the admitted dependencies and forced relation is present.

exact_result: The complete reported experimental exponent interval contains exactly one positive integer exponent, two, agreeing with the independently sealed inverse-square law.
induction_base: The first positive integer receives one exact below, inside or above interval decision.
induction_step: Advance by one positive successor until the candidate exceeds the upper endpoint; every later positive integer is then also above it, closing the family without a completed infinite object.
exclusions: no measured result used by the formal inverse-square derivation
no logarithm, regression, floating fit or best-match selection in the checker
no semantic numerical zero, negative, irrational or imaginary proof value
no omission of the reported central value or uncertainty
no claim that interval agreement proves an exact physical value
operational_witnesses: The complete exact reported interval contains only positive integer exponent two.
The first positive integer lies strictly below the reported interval.
The third positive integer lies strictly above the reported interval.
falsification_condition: The complete registered reported interval does not contain exponent two, contains another positive integer exponent, differs from its source hash, is opened into the formal derivation, or a tampered comparison is accepted.
